A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAC-labeling work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, seven tables, six figures, and Appendix A are readable and support a complete comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original PAC-labeling evaluations on text, image, and protein tasks in Section 4, plus experiments comparing asymptotic and nonasymptotic bounds in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including calibration, multi-model routing, and the additional results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and Section 3 retain the same threshold selection, uncertainty calibration, differentiable routing, uncertainty learning, and cost-sensitive objectives. The added discussion of compatibility with other annotation schemes does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate media bias, global-warming stance, misinformation, ImageNet, ImageNet v2, sentiment analysis, and protein structure prediction. The calibration, routing, and appendix experiments retain the same task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain fixed-threshold labeling, AI-only labeling, individual GPT-4o and Claude models, and asymptotic versus nonasymptotic PAC labeling. Newly discussed methods such as CoAnnotating and MCAL are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same losses, epsilon settings, alpha = 0.05, models, calibration setup, and prediction costs. Betting bounds remain used for discrete-label and routing experiments, while continuous-label and appendix experiments retain CLT bounds.

E4.justification: The uncertainty-calibration comparison in Table 4, routing loss-curve analysis, and asymptotic-bound comparison in Appendix A are unchanged. The routing loss plot moves from Figure 4 to Figure 5 without adding or removing an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 repetitions, means and standard deviations of savings, the 95th percentile of empirical error, and plots showing 50 randomly chosen trials. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–7 and the matched figure contents are unchanged. For example, Table 5 retains the router's 41.61 ± 1.50% budget saving and 4.61% error. Swapping Figures 4 and 5 changes presentation only.

T1.justification: The PAC definition, threshold construction, Theorem 1 and its proof, Corollary 1, and routing-gradient derivations are retained. Additional statements emphasizing nonasymptotic validity restate the existing guarantee rather than introduce new assumptions or mathematics.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain guaranteed low-error labeling with reduced expert cost, uncertainty calibration, and multi-model routing. v2 foregrounds nonasymptotic validity and independence from uncertainty-score quality, but these properties were already stated or established in v1.

C2.justification: Section 1.2 adds a concrete interpretation of PAC labeling as a validity wrapper that can select CoAnnotating's annotation budget k. It also explicitly states that PAC-quality labels are neither necessary nor sufficient for active learning. Existing result interpretations and Appendix A's asymptotic-error caveat remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same code-access link, prediction and uncertainty construction details, five calibration groups with three bins, and model-cost values. No additional implementation settings or reproducibility resources are disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially expands research positioning beyond v1's broad connections. It explicitly contrasts assumptions and guarantees, discusses CoAnnotating, WANLI, and SynthBio, and broadens coverage of noisy-label aggregation and control-variate inference. Twelve references are added and two removed; the changes extend beyond citation renumbering.

P1.justification: The abstract and opening motivation are revised around scientific data providers, related work gains three topical headings, and short explanatory statements emphasize the existing guarantee. These changes are concentrated in the opening sections; the overall section sequence and most technical and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Existing displays are rearranged: Figure 1 appears before the proof, algorithm boxes and Table 5 shift position, and Figures 4 and 5 exchange order. The routing loss plot is also reduced in size. Figure contents and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves contextual clarity by replacing broad related-work connections with explicit comparisons of assumptions and guarantees, including a concrete explanation of compatibility with CoAnnotating. The opening also distinguishes validity from the cost-saving benefits of informative uncertainty scores more clearly. These are useful, limited improvements; the methods, proofs, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
